findings.headline: 6 of 17 documented 99214/99215 claims (35%) documented below billed level; peer rate 4%
findings.interpretation: Bills 99215 on 21.7% of claims when 2.4% is expected (z_adj 7.55). 65% of its 99215s are on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions. All 3 sampled 99215s were documented at moderate MDM. Random sample of 30 is complete; draft overpayment estimate $2,703 (CI $2,143-$3,262). Needs a certified coder to re-score the charts.

findings.headline: 7 of 13 documented 99215 claims (54%) documented below billed level; peer rate 0%
findings.interpretation: This panel really is sicker (expected 99215 share 10.2%, and most 99215s are on patients with 5+ conditions). Even so, it bills 39% 99215 and is about 2x the peer share at every complexity level. Over half the sampled 99215 charts support only moderate MDM. Random sample of 30 is complete; draft estimate $2,300 (CI $1,343-$3,256). The sick panel explains some of the excess but not what the charts show.

findings.headline: 5 of 7 documented 99215 claims (71%) documented below billed level; peer rate 0%
findings.interpretation: 22.3% 99215 against 4.2% expected (z_adj 5.45). 43% of its 99215s are on patients with 0-1 conditions. Chart rule triggered (8/30 below billed). Random sample complete; draft estimate $2,431 (CI $1,442-$3,419).

findings.headline: 3 of 6 documented 99215 claims (50%) documented below billed level; 88% of 99215s on patients with 0-1 conditions
findings.interpretation: 17.2% 99215 against 1.7% expected (z_adj 7.15), mostly on low-complexity patients. The chart evidence is thinner (3/30 below billed overall; chart rule not triggered, summary rule only), so this is the weakest of the four upcoding leanings. Draft estimate $819 (CI $242-$1,397). Treat as lower priority, and confirm with a larger sample before recovery.
